content_voiceover: This table compares the 2020 European LeukemiaNet and 2023 NCCN criteria for stopping TKI therapy in chronic myeloid leukemia, a common boards topic called treatment free remission. Mandatory requirements for both guidelines include being in chronic phase disease, a motivated and well informed patient, access to high quality quantitative PCR on the international scale with rapid turnaround, and structured monitoring, monthly for the first six months, every two months through month twelve, then every three months after. For stopping to be allowed, the patient should be on first line therapy, or second line if the switch was due to intolerance, have a typical e13a2 or e14a2 BCR colon colon ABL1 transcript, and have been on TKI therapy for more than five years, with a deep molecular response, MR4 or better, for more than two years. NCCN is similar but only requires three years of therapy. Stopping is more strongly recommended when TKI duration exceeds five years and deep molecular response, MR4.5, has been sustained for more than two years.
keypoints: Mandatory: chronic phase, motivated patient, quantitative PCR, structured monitoring
Stop allowed: first line therapy, typical transcript, over five years of TKI
Stop recommended: over five years TKI with MR4.5 for over two years
NCCN allows earlier stopping consideration, at three years of TKI therapy
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the framework: mandatory criteria ensure safe monitoring, stop allowed criteria set the minimum bar of five years TKI therapy and two years deep molecular response, and stop recommended criteria require an even deeper and more durable response. NCCN is slightly more permissive, allowing consideration at three years of therapy instead of five.
